sources.title: Firefly
sources.observation: The source says fireflies emit light mainly during twilight to attract mates. It adds that light production in Lampyridae is thought to have originated as a warning signal that the larvae were distasteful, and was later co-opted as a mating signal. It also notes that some adult female Photuris fireflies mimic other species’ flash patterns to lure males as prey.

sources.title: Studies on the flash communication system in Photinus fireflies
sources.observation: The author argues that in Photinus fireflies, bioluminescent flashes function as a courtship communication system: flying males emit species-specific flash patterns, and receptive females respond with species-typical reply flashes after characteristic delays, enabling mate recognition and localization. The study reports that different Photinus species use distinct flash patterns and timing, supporting their role in species-specific mating signals.
